name: Yellowtail
notes: Up to 5 of the 10 may be under 24 in fork length. Boat fillets: min 17 in, max 10 fillets under 17 in, each with 1-in square skin patch. Same rule for divers and boats.

name: Pacific bonito
size: 24 in FL or 5 lb (up to 5 under)
notes: Up to 5 fish may be under 24 in FL OR under 5 lb. Boat fillets: max 10 fillets of any length, all count against the 5-undersized tolerance, 1-in square skin patch each.

name: California barracuda
notes: No undersized tolerance. Boat fillets: min 17 in w/ 1 in sq patch of silver skin. AL (§1.62) = base of 1st dorsal spine to end of longest tail lobe; used when the head is removed, tail must stay on.

name: Mackerel (Pacific & jack)
notes: Booklet lists Pacific (chub) and jack mackerel as one row under §27.60(b). Not counted toward the 20-fish general limit.

name: Dorado (dolphinfish)
notes: No species-specific section; general limit applies. Boat fillets any size with 1-in square skin patch (§27.65(b)(13)). Classed as highly migratory species.

name: Albacore
bag: 10 S of Pt Conception (25 N); extra to 20 general
notes: Special limit in addition to the 20-fish general limit. Boat fillets S of Pt Conception: each fish bagged separately, bag marked with species name, cut into 6 pieces w/ all skin (4 loins, collar w/ both pectorals, belly w/ vent & both pelvics).

name: Bluefin tuna
notes: Limit applies to all bluefin possessed regardless of where taken (incl. Mexican waters). Boat fillets S of Pt Conception: each fish individually bagged, bag marked w/ species, cut into 6 pieces with all skin attached.

name: Skipjack tuna
notes: Not counted toward the 20-fish general limit. Same 6-piece bagging rule as other tunas if filleted on a boat S of Pt Conception (§27.65(b)(11)).

name: Yellowfin/bigeye/other tuna
notes: CDFW regulates yellowfin, bigeye and all other unlisted tunas as one 10-fish row; unlike albacore/bluefin these count toward the 20-fish total. Boat fillets S of Pt Conception: 6-piece bagging rule w/ all skin attached.

name: Wahoo
notes: Not individually listed in the 2026 booklet; general 10-per-species limit under §27.60(a) applies (also 10 if treated as 'other tuna' under §28.38(d)). Boat fillets: any size, 1-in skin patch.

name: Striped marlin
notes: §28.95: spears, harpoons or bow gear may not be aboard any vessel on a day or trip when marlin has been taken. Booklet: marlin is not allowed for commercial take. Classed as highly migratory species.

name: Broadbill swordfish
spear: PROHIBITED by spear (hook and line only)
notes: §28.90 excludes broadbill from spearfishing take; §28.95 also bars bow and arrow and bars spears/harpoons aboard any vessel on a day or trip when swordfish has been taken.

name: Jacksmelt
notes: Not counted toward the 20-fish general limit. Bait species.

name: Topsmelt
notes: Not counted toward the 20-fish general limit. May also be taken with dip nets of any size or baited hoop nets up to 36 in (§28.80). Bait species.

name: Pacific sardine
notes: Not counted toward the 20-fish general limit. Bait species. 2026 domoic acid consumption advisories were issued in-season for Monterey Bay only (not SoCal); check the Inseason page.

name: Northern anchovy
notes: Not counted toward the 20-fish general limit. Dip net/baited hoop net up to 36 in allowed (§28.80). 2026 domoic acid take restrictions (Sept 11, 2026) apply to Monterey Bay only, not SoCal; check the Inseason page.
